target_customer: Dairy and infant formula manufacturers and food brands that would license or buy cell-cultured milk
problem: Conventional dairy carries a large carbon footprint and animal welfare costs, and plant milks do not match dairy nutrition or taste. The company wants to make real milk from mammalian cells without cows.
business_model: Biotech product company targeting B2B supply of cultivated milk and ingredients, plus licensing; pre-revenue at the time of the seed round

founders.name: Sohail Gupta
founders.background_notes: YC page: 9+ years in food and healthcare across India, the USA and the Middle East. TechCrunch says he is vegetarian and the idea came from a search for a nutritious alternative during his wife's pregnancy.

founders.name: Avhijeet Kapoor
education: IIT Delhi, biotechnology with a minor in computer science
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists consulting for Epigamia, Novartis and Milkbasket.

founders.name: Bhavna Tandon
education: Rice University, PhD in molecular biology and biochemistry
founders.background_notes: YC page: 3+ years as a scientist on cell culture and model organisms.

competitors.name: Perfect Day
competitors.what: Animal-free dairy proteins made by fermentation

competitors.name: Wilk
competitors.what: Israeli maker of cell-cultured cow and human milk components
competitors.traction_then: Planned products by 2024; pilot with Tara Dairy

competitors.name: TurtleTree Labs
competitors.what: Cell-cultured human breastmilk, later cow milk

competitors.name: Biomilq
competitors.what: Cell-cultured human milk from mammary cells
competitors.funding_then: 3.5M USD in June (year per snippet unclear, around 2021)

competitors.name: Better Dairy
competitors.what: Dairy-free cheese and dairy from precision fermentation

technical_complexity.rationale: Growing bovine mammary cells to produce whole milk at scale is research-grade bioprocess work; the company said in 2022 a product was a few years away.

defensibility.rationale: The YC page cites a patent held by a founder, and regulatory approval for cultivated dairy is a barrier, but several funded rivals pursued the same approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying the company through the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in June 2022 described a large dairy market and growing investor interest in animal-free dairy; the company itself cites a 700B USD dairy market and an 80B USD infant formula market (YC page).

branding.domain_note: Product site is unrealmilk.com rather than a brownfoods domain; company name Brown Foods and product brand UnReal Milk are separate.

identity.logo: Milk bottle imagery per the site

branding.brand_signature: UnReal Milk product name playing on real milk made without a cow
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage from Forbes, TechCrunch, Fast Company and Entrepreneur is displayed on the site; no fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The product name is memorable and drew press, but no source shows community or merch; the company name is generic.

outcome_analysis: Brown Foods raised a small seed round in June 2022 from YC and food tech investors and unveiled its lab made whole cow milk in February 2025. It is still active, pre-revenue as far as sources show, and faces long regulatory approval timelines and funded rivals. No later rounds were found, so its trajectory is unresolved.
notes: Round confirmed by TechCrunch and AgFunder. Green Queen reports a 1M USD pre-seed, seen in one outlet and unverified. CB Insights shows about 2.86M total, unverified. Founder education and employers are from the YC page. TechCrunch lists Miruku, EVERY, NotCo and Climax Foods as peers but only the dated rivals above were listed.
